problem_statement: On RISC-V, when an essential thread aborts itself, the fatal error handling path cannot return: the architecture's fatal error handler is treated as non-returning (a tail call with no recovery), so an essential thread that aborts itself cannot be handled by the system's fatal error handler and then recover to continue running. As a result, the self-abort of an essential thread is not handled correctly on RISC-V the way it is on other architectures. The fatal error path on RISC-V should be able to return to reschedule when the fatal error handler is invoked in a context (such as an essential thread aborting itself) where the kernel chooses to continue rather than terminate.
